prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and policies

Economy and taxes
- Eliminate the deficit, then run a surplus; continue annual NHS spending increases.
- No rises in VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax rates.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000.
- Crack down on tax evasion/avoidance; strengthen the Office of Tax Simplification.

Jobs and business
- Create 2 million jobs and 3 million apprenticeships; aim for highest G7 employment rate.
- Employment measures for young people, including a time‑limited Youth Allowance linked to work, training or community work.
- Maintain competitive business taxes; review business rates; reduce regulation; expand Start Up Loans; prompt payment and SME procurement targets.

Welfare and family support
- Roll out Universal Credit; reduce the household benefit cap to £23,000.
- Freeze most working-age benefits for two years (with exemptions).
- Tax‑Free Childcare up to £2,000 per child; 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds.

Housing and planning
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for first‑time buyers under 40).
- Extend Help to Buy and introduce a Help to Buy ISA.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; prioritise brownfield development; protect the Green Belt.
- Deliver 275,000 additional affordable homes by 2020.

Health and social care
- Fund the NHS Five Year Forward View with at least £8bn extra by 2020.
- 7‑day GP and hospital services; same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s.
- Integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs; expand mental health access; strengthen cancer and dementia strategies; digital records and access.

Education and skills
- Protect per‑pupil funding; raise literacy/numeracy standards; core academic GCSEs.
- Convert failing/coasting schools to academies; open at least 500 more free schools.
- Recruit more maths/physics teachers; expand University Technical Colleges and National Colleges.
- Remove the cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans; publish teaching quality data.

Infrastructure and regions
- Invest over £100bn in infrastructure: HS2/HS3, Crossrail, rail electrification, £15bn roads, cycling.
- Freeze regulated rail fares in real terms; smart ticketing; better compensation.
- Superfast broadband to 95% by 2017; expand mobile coverage; prepare for 5G.
- Devolve powers and budgets in England; develop a Northern Powerhouse.

Immigration
- Reform EU welfare access (e.g., 4‑year residency for in‑work benefits; limits on jobseeker benefits).
- Maintain the non‑EU skilled migration cap; strengthen enforcement, exit checks, landlord checks.
- Establish a Controlling Migration Fund; English fluency requirement for public‑facing roles.

Energy and environment
- Promote competition; smart meters by 2020; insulate 1m homes.
- Support nuclear, offshore wind, CCS; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Support shale with community benefits and a northern wealth fund; back North Sea sector.
- Create a UK/Overseas Territories “Blue Belt”; plant 11m trees; improve air/water quality; expand flood defences.

Crime, justice, and security
- Continue police reform; expand cyber capability; update stop and search and complaints systems.
- Modernise prisons; focus on rehabilitation; tougher action on legal highs and alcohol‑related offending.
- Strengthen victims’ rights with a Victims’ Law.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights; modernise courts and legal aid.

Counter‑extremism
- Update communications data and interception laws with oversight.
- New powers to restrict extremist organisations and individuals; prevent extremist platforms.

Pensions and retirement
- Maintain the triple lock; introduce the single‑tier pension; retain pensioner benefits.
- Pension freedoms and tax changes to ease inheritance.
- Increase effective Inheritance Tax threshold for the family home to £1m (funded by reduced relief for very high earners).

Union, EU, and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
- Hold an in‑out EU referendum by end‑2017 after renegotiation; protect non‑Eurozone interests; pursue trade deals.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (including successor nuclear deterrent); invest in equipment and cyber; uphold the Armed Forces Covenant.
- Keep international development at 0.7% of income, focusing on health, education, water/sanitation, gender equality, and crisis response.

Culture, sport, society, and government
- Free entry to national museums; support creative industries and anti‑piracy measures; freeze BBC licence fee pending review.
- Fund school and community sports; host major events.
- Expand National Citizen Service; three days’ paid volunteering leave in large firms/public sector.
- Cut government waste; expand digital services and transparency; boundary reforms; tackle voter fraud and introduce votes for life.
